title: Obstetric Blood Availability And Time-To-Transfusion Gaps In LMICs
summary: Build a verified facility-level evidence workflow for measuring whether women with life-threatening obstetric haemorrhage can obtain safe, compatible blood in time, separating national donation volume from real service availability, stock interruption, referral delay, and transfusion readiness.
why_it_matters: WHO reports about 70,000 deaths from postpartum haemorrhage each year, while its 2026 blood-safety data show a median of 4.5 donations per 1,000 people in low-income countries and explicitly warn that many patients lack timely access to safe blood. A ministry of health blood-service director and maternal-health director need facility-level evidence on where the failure occurs: collection, testing, storage, transport, cross-match, staffing, or referral. Verified evidence would change procurement, cold-chain, hub-and-spoke, emergency referral, and facility-readiness priorities. National donation totals alone cannot answer that decision.

success_metrics.target: Every accepted source distinguishes national blood supply from facility-level availability, interruption, readiness, or time-to-transfusion evidence.
success_metrics.validation_method: Reviewer checks source grain, indicator definitions, numerator, denominator, and time reference in evidence.json and datasets.md.

success_metrics.target: A reviewed artifact names the health-system decision, facility level, geography, and time window it can inform without becoming a clinical protocol.
success_metrics.validation_method: Field-reality reviewer checks the named user, decision, timing, and explicit non-use cases before publication.

success_metrics.target: No operational blood-allocation or clinical recommendation is accepted without domain review, red-team review, and independent replication.
success_metrics.validation_method: Validate task status, reviewer roles, replication records, and publication gates before accepting any quantitative output.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, transfusion-medicine and maternal-health domain review, red-team review for harmful allocation or clinical interpretation, and independent replication for quantitative outputs.
